inertia_definition_correction.rigid_body: sum of inertias reflected to same axis side for common angular acceleration
inertia_definition_correction.relative_torsional_mode: Jm*Jl/(Jm+Jl), used only in two-mass relative torsion coordinate

simulation.anti_windup: back calculation, tracking time constant 30 ms
simulation.integration: RK4; 2 substeps/sample for tracking tests and 4 substeps/sample for step tests

notch_bank.implementation: second-order SOS, prewarped bilinear/Tustin; applied in speed-PI torque-command path

speed_feedback_lowpass.implementation: bilinear transform; applied to motor-speed feedback measurement path

margin_method: nested SISO motor-speed and load-position loops; continuous flexible plant FRF; digital SOS responses; 1 ms feedback delay plus half-sample/ZOH approximation; all gain/phase crossover values retained
limitations: All inertias, stiffness, damping, controller settings, noise, torque limits, filter settings and disturbances are synthetic
Rigid-body inertia is distinct from relative-mode reduced inertia; previous erroneous gain values are superseded
No PMSM electrical dynamics, inverter switching, bus jitter, encoder quantization, multi-axis MIMO coupling or measured thermal law
A torque-command notch can reduce feedback correction against external disturbance at the notch frequency
Low-pass filter adds feedback phase/group delay; magnitude attenuation alone is not an acceptance criterion
Multiple crossovers require Nyquist/closed-loop checks; classical SISO GM/PM is not MIMO disk margin
No real device data, HIL, bench or machine validation
